works.description: Kittler argues that around 1900 the gramophone, film and typewriter split what writing once held together into three separate data streams, sound, image and text, recorded by machines without passing through human sense or meaning. 'Media determine our situation': what we can perceive and say depends on the technical systems that store it.
works.description_zh: 基特勒认为，1900 年前后，留声机、电影和打字机把书写曾经统一承载的东西拆成三条独立的数据流：声音、图像和文字，由机器直接记录，不再经过人的感官与意义。“媒介决定我们的处境”：我们能感知和言说什么，取决于存储它们的技术系统。
works.idea_en: Recording machines do not extend the human senses so much as replace them with technical inscription; noise and nonsense are stored as faithfully as speech.
works.idea_zh: 记录机器与其说是延伸了人的感官，不如说是用技术铭写取代了它们：噪音和无意义的声音与言语一样被忠实保存。
works.method: Media-archaeological readings of literature, psychoanalysis and engineering texts, arranged around the three devices; German edition Brinkmann & Bose, 1986; English translation by Geoffrey Winthrop-Young and Michael Wutz, Stanford University Press, 1999.
works.method_zh: 围绕三种装置，对文学、精神分析与工程文献进行媒介考古式的解读；德文版 1986 年由 Brinkmann & Bose 出版，英译本由 Geoffrey Winthrop-Young 与 Michael Wutz 翻译，斯坦福大学出版社 1999 年出版。

paper.venue: Brinkmann & Bose, 1986; English: Stanford University Press, 1999
paper.title: Gramophone, Film, Typewriter

works.title_zh: 留声机 电影 打字机

works.title: Very Nervous System
works.description: An interactive sound installation in which video cameras watch a visitor moving through an empty room, and a computer turns every gesture into sound and music in real time.
works.description_zh: 一件交互声音装置：摄像机注视着在空房间里走动的访客，计算机把每一个动作实时转化为声音和音乐。
works.idea_en: An invisible, room-sized interface makes the whole body the input, so the loop between movement and machine response is felt rather than operated.
works.idea_zh: 看不见、充满整个房间的界面把整个身体变成输入，人与机器之间的反馈回路成了被感受而不是被操作的东西。
works.method: Video cameras feed image processors and a computer that measure changes of movement across the space and drive synthesizers and a sound system; Rokeby later released the system as the softVNS software.
works.method_zh: 摄像机把画面送入图像处理器和计算机，测量空间中动作的变化，再驱动合成器和音响系统；Rokeby 后来把这套系统发布为 softVNS 软件。
exhibited: Prix Ars Electronica 1991, Award of Distinction (Interactive Art)

works.title: A Manifesto for Cyborgs: Science, Technology, and Socialist Feminism in the 1980s
works.description: Haraway's essay takes the cyborg, a hybrid of machine and organism, as an ironic political myth for feminism, after the boundaries between human and animal, organism and machine, and physical and non-physical have broken down.
works.description_zh: Haraway 的这篇文章把赛博格（机器与有机体的混合体）当作女性主义的反讽政治神话；它出现在人与动物、有机体与机器、物质与非物质的边界已经崩塌之后。
works.idea_en: The cyborg refuses origins and purity, which makes human–machine hybridity a political opening rather than a loss.
works.idea_zh: 赛博格拒绝起源与纯粹，这让人机混杂成为政治上的出口，而不是损失。
works.method: Political essay mixing socialist feminism, science studies and science fiction; reprinted in Simians, Cyborgs, and Women (1991).
works.method_zh: 融合社会主义女性主义、科学研究与科幻的政治文章；收入《Simians, Cyborgs, and Women》（1991）。

paper.venue: Socialist Review 80, 1985; in Simians, Cyborgs, and Women (Routledge, 1991)
paper.title: Simians, Cyborgs, and Women: The Reinvention of Nature

works.title_zh: 赛博格宣言：20世纪80年代的科学、技术与社会主义女性主义

works.title: Racter: The Policeman's Beard Is Half Constructed
works.description: A book presented as the first ever written by a computer, the prose-generating program Racter, full of strange, passionate sentences about love, electricity and steak.
works.description_zh: 一本号称第一部由计算机写成的书，作者是散文生成程序 Racter，书中满是关于爱、电和牛排的怪异而激昂的句子。
works.idea_en: Long before large language models, the claim of machine authorship already depended on human editing and on our wish to hear a voice.
works.idea_zh: 早在大语言模型之前，“机器作者”的说法就已经依赖人类的编辑，以及我们想听到一个声音的愿望。
works.method: A rule- and template-based generator written by William Chamberlain and Thomas Etter; the published text was selected from its output.
works.method_zh: 由 William Chamberlain 与 Thomas Etter 编写的基于规则和模板的生成器；出版文本是从其输出中挑选出来的。

works.title: The Hands
works.description: A pair of controllers strapped to the hands, with keys, tilt switches and an ultrasound sensor measuring the distance between them, with which Waisvisz played electronic sound through gesture for more than twenty years.
works.description_zh: 一对绑在双手上的控制器，带按键、倾斜开关和测量双手距离的超声传感器；Waisvisz 用它以手势演奏电子声音二十余年。
works.idea_en: An instrument worn on the body makes electronic sound physical again: effort and gesture become audible.
works.idea_zh: 穿在身上的乐器让电子声音重新变得有身体感：力气与姿态变得可听。
works.method: Hand-mounted sensors built at STEIM, sending MIDI to synthesisers and later to STEIM's LiSa live-sampling software.
works.method_zh: 在 STEIM 制作的手戴传感器，向合成器（后来是 STEIM 的 LiSa 实时采样软件）发送 MIDI。

works.title: Vehicles: Experiments in Synthetic Psychology
works.description: A series of fourteen imaginary vehicles, each a little more complex, whose sensors wired straight or crossed to their motors make them look afraid, aggressive, in love or curious.
works.description_zh: 十四辆逐步复杂的想象小车：传感器与电机平行或交叉连接，就让它们看起来害怕、好斗、恋爱或好奇。
works.idea_en: Behaviour that is easy to build is hard to analyse from outside, so observers read minds into simple machines.
works.idea_zh: 容易造出来的行为，从外部却很难分析，于是观察者会把心智读进简单的机器里。
works.method: Thought experiments in "synthetic psychology": build first, then interpret; widely rebuilt as robots and simulations.
works.method_zh: “合成心理学”思想实验：先造，再解释；后来被大量做成机器人和模拟程序。
keywords: law of uphill analysis and downhill invention

paper.title: Vehicles: Experiments in Synthetic Psychology

works.title: Text Tones
works.description: Six white plinths carry aluminium tubes struck by small hammers. A microphone takes in the sounds of the gallery, voices, footsteps, closing doors, and the sculpture plays them back through the tubes, so whatever is said in the room returns as a monotone reflection at the tubes' own pitches.
works.description_zh: 六个白色底座上装着由小锤敲击的铝管。麦克风收录展厅里的声音，人声、脚步、关门声，雕塑再通过铝管把它们放出来，于是房间里说的一切都以铝管自身音高的单调回声返回。
works.idea_en: A listening machine hears everything and keeps only what fits its own body; speech comes back as the resonance of a tube.
works.idea_zh: 会听的机器什么都听见，却只留下符合它自身身体的部分：言语回来时，成了一根管子的共振。
works.method: Microphone input is stored and split into an analog and a digital signal: the digital signal drives pairs of hammers striking each tube while the analog signal plays through a loudspeaker into the tube; tube lengths divide two octaves into five intervals. Originally tape-based, later reworked with sensors and a computer.
works.method_zh: 麦克风收录的声音被存储并分成模拟和数字两路信号：数字信号驱动成对的小锤敲击铝管，模拟信号则通过扬声器送入管内；各管长度把两个八度分成五个音程。最初用磁带，后来改为传感器加计算机。

works.title: Towards a Philosophy of Photography
works.description: Flusser describes the camera as an apparatus, a black box whose program the photographer only plays inside, producing "technical images" that realise possibilities already written into the device.
works.description_zh: Flusser 把相机描述为一种“装置”：一个黑箱，摄影师只是在它的程序内游戏，产出的“技术图像”不过实现了设备中早已写好的可能性。
works.idea_en: Whoever uses an apparatus is also used by its program; this applies directly to generative models.
works.idea_zh: 使用装置的人也被其程序所使用；这一点可以直接套用到生成模型上。
works.method: Short philosophical essay; German original Für eine Philosophie der Fotografie (European Photography, 1983).
works.method_zh: 一部简短的哲学论著；德文原版《Für eine Philosophie der Fotografie》（European Photography，1983）。

paper.title: Towards a Philosophy of Photography

works.title: Blade Runner
works.description: Replicants with implanted memories and four-year lifespans are hunted by a detective who tests them for empathy; the last one dies saying his memories will be lost 'like tears in rain'.
works.description_zh: 拥有植入记忆和四年寿命的复制人被一名侦探追捕，他用共情测试来识别它们；最后一个复制人临死前说，他的记忆将会消逝，“如同雨中的泪水”。
works.idea_en: If a made being has memories and fears death, the test that separates it from us becomes the real question.
works.idea_zh: 如果一个被制造出来的存在拥有记忆并害怕死亡，那么把它与我们区分开的测试本身就成了真正的问题。
works.method: Film by Ridley Scott, adapted from Philip K. Dick's novel Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? (1968).
works.method_zh: Ridley Scott 执导，改编自菲利普·K·迪克的小说《仿生人会梦见电子羊吗？》（1968）。

works.title: The First Accident of the Twenty-First Century
works.description: For his 1982 Whitney Museum retrospective, Paik walked Robot K-456 onto Madison Avenue, where it was struck by a car in a staged 'traffic accident'. In 2026 the restored robot walked again in a performance marking 20 years since Paik's death.
works.description_zh: 在 1982 年惠特尼美术馆回顾展期间，白南准让《机器人 K-456》走上麦迪逊大道，被一辆汽车撞倒，上演了一场“交通事故”。2026 年，修复后的机器人在纪念白南准逝世 20 周年的表演中再次行走。
works.idea_en: Staging a machine's death in public turns a robot into something that can be mourned.
works.idea_zh: 在公共空间上演机器之死，让机器人成为可以被哀悼的对象。
works.method: Street performance: the remote-controlled robot is driven into traffic and hit by a car at low speed, then displayed damaged.
works.method_zh: 街头表演：遥控机器人被驶入车流，被低速行驶的汽车撞倒，之后以损坏状态展出。
exhibited: Nam June Paik retrospective, Whitney Museum of American Art 1982
Nam June Paik Art Center, 20th memorial performance 2026
works.title_zh: 二十一世纪的第一起事故

works.title: Golem XIV
works.description: A fictional lecture course given to humans by a superintelligent military computer that has lost interest in war and explains how limited human minds are, before falling silent.
works.description_zh: 一部虚构的讲座集：一台对战争失去兴趣的超级智能军用计算机向人类授课，解释人类心智有多么有限，然后陷入沉默。
works.idea_en: A superior machine mind may simply not care about us, and its indifference is the most unsettling part.
works.idea_zh: 一个更高级的机器心智也许根本不在乎我们，而这种漠然才是最令人不安的。
works.method: A philosophical essay in the form of science fiction: introductions, memos and two lectures attributed to the computer.
works.method_zh: 以科幻形式写成的哲学随笔：由导言、备忘录和两篇归于这台计算机的讲座组成。

works.title: The Buddha in the Robot
works.description: A book in which Mori argues, from Zen Buddhism, that robots have the Buddha-nature and that building them is a way to understand the self.
works.description_zh: 森政弘在书中从禅宗出发指出：机器人同样具有佛性，制造机器人也是理解自我的一种途径。
works.idea_en: A non-Western frame in which machines are not opposed to spirit but part of the same continuum.
works.idea_zh: 一个非西方的框架：机器不与心灵对立，而处在同一个连续体中。
works.method: A collection of essays and talks by a robotics engineer, translated from Japanese and published by Kosei Publishing (Tokyo).
works.method_zh: 一位机器人工程师的随笔与讲演集，由日文译出，东京佼成出版社出版。

paper.title: The Buddha in the Robot: A Robot Engineer's Thoughts on Science and Religion

works.title: Hole in Space
works.description: For three evenings, life-size live video screens linked passers-by at Lincoln Center in New York and a shopping centre in Century City, Los Angeles, via satellite, with no signs or explanation; strangers, then families, met across the continent.
works.description_zh: 连续三个晚上，真人大小的实时视频屏幕通过卫星把纽约林肯中心和洛杉矶世纪城购物中心的路人连接起来，没有任何标识或说明；陌生人、后来是家人，隔着大陆相遇。
works.idea_en: A telecom link becomes a public place: people invent how to behave with remote bodies as soon as they meet them.
works.idea_zh: 通信链路变成了公共场所：人们一遇见远方的身体，就当场发明与之相处的方式。
works.method: Two-way satellite video link with cameras and rear-projection screens in shop windows on each coast.
works.method_zh: 双向卫星视频链路，两岸各在橱窗中安装摄像机和背投屏幕。

works.title: Minds, Brains, and Programs
works.description: Searle's Chinese Room: a person who knows no Chinese follows a rulebook to return fluent Chinese answers, which shows, he argues, that running a program is not the same as understanding.
works.description_zh: Searle 的“中文屋”：一个不懂中文的人照着规则手册给出流利的中文回答；他据此论证，运行程序并不等于理解。
works.idea_en: Fluent output does not prove a mind behind it, which is exactly the question chatbots now raise.
works.idea_zh: 流畅的输出并不证明背后有心智，这正是今天的聊天机器人重新提出的问题。
works.method: Thought experiment published with open peer commentaries and Searle's replies.
works.method_zh: 一个思想实验，与多篇同行公开评论及 Searle 的回应一同发表。

paper.title: Minds, Brains, and Programs

works.title: Telexistence (TELESAR)
works.description: Tachi's concept and robot series in which an operator wearing a head-mounted display and haptic suit sees, hears and feels through a remote humanoid robot as if present in its body; TELESAR V (2011) adds fine touch.
works.description_zh: 馆暲提出的概念及其机器人系列：操作者戴上头戴显示器和触觉装置，通过远方的人形机器人去看、听和感受，仿佛身处它的身体中；2011 年的 TELESAR V 加入了精细触觉。
works.idea_en: A robot can be designed not as another agent but as a second body the human inhabits.
works.idea_zh: 机器人可以不被设计成另一个主体，而是人所“住进”的第二个身体。
works.method: Stereo cameras on the robot head follow the operator's head motion; master-slave arms and hands transmit force, vibration and temperature back to the operator.
works.method_zh: 机器人头部的立体摄像头跟随操作者的头部运动；主从式手臂与手把力、振动和温度反馈给操作者。

paper.title: Telexistence: Enabling Humans to Be Virtually Ubiquitous

works.title: Third Hand
works.description: A mechanical right hand attached to Stelarc's arm and driven by the electrical signals of his abdominal and leg muscles, which he wrote and performed with alongside his own two hands for many years.
works.description_zh: 一只安装在 Stelarc 手臂上的机械右手，由他腹部和腿部肌肉的电信号驱动；多年来他用它与自己的双手一起写字和表演。
works.idea_en: An extra limb is learned, not given: the body slowly makes room for a machine that it controls indirectly.
works.idea_zh: 多出来的肢体需要学习而非天生：身体慢慢为一台间接控制的机器腾出位置。
works.method: Robotic hand with pinch, grasp and wrist rotation, controlled by EMG electrodes on abdomen and legs, with tactile feedback to the arm.
works.method_zh: 具备捏、握和手腕旋转功能的机械手，由腹部和腿部的肌电电极控制，并向手臂提供触觉反馈。

works.title: SRL machine performances
works.description: In vacant lots and under freeways, huge home-built machines, flame-throwers, walking robots and remote-controlled vehicles fight, burn and dismantle each other and props in front of crowds, in shows such as A Plan for Social Improvement (1988) and Illusions of Shameless Abundance (1989).
works.description_zh: 在空地和高架桥下，巨大的自制机器、喷火器、步行机器人和遥控车辆当着人群互相搏斗、焚烧，拆毁彼此和道具，如 A Plan for Social Improvement（1988）和 Illusions of Shameless Abundance（1989）。
works.idea_en: Machines built only to attack each other reveal the violence and spectacle inside industrial and military technology.
works.idea_zh: 只为互相攻击而造的机器，揭示了工业与军事技术内部的暴力和景观。
works.method: Mark Pauline's team rebuilds industrial and military surplus into remote-controlled and semi-autonomous machines, operated live by crews during the shows.
works.method_zh: Mark Pauline 的团队把工业和军用剩余物资改装成遥控和半自主机器，演出时由操作组现场操控。
exhibited: A Plan for Social Improvement, Amsterdam 1988

works.title: Die Mensch-Maschine (The Man-Machine) and the robots
works.description: On the album Die Mensch-Maschine, Kraftwerk sing 'we are the robots' through vocoders; they had mannequin doubles of themselves made, and in later concerts robot dummies performed The Robots on stage in their place.
works.description_zh: 在专辑 Die Mensch-Maschine 中，Kraftwerk 用声码器唱着“我们是机器人”；他们为自己制作了人偶替身，后来的演唱会上则由机器人假人代替他们在台上表演《机器人》。
works.idea_en: Pop can make the fusion of human and machine desirable; the robot doubles also question who the performer is.
works.idea_zh: 流行音乐能让人与机器的融合变得令人向往；机器人替身也让人追问：谁才是表演者。
works.method: Vocoders and synthesisers, choreographed stiff movement, and mechanised mannequins of the four members.
works.method_zh: 声码器与合成器、编排好的僵硬动作，以及四名成员的机械化人偶。

works.title: Machine Vision
works.description: An installation in which video cameras on slowly rotating motorised mounts, one pair aimed at a mirrored sphere, scan the room and show it on monitors from viewpoints no human eye occupies.
works.description_zh: 一件装置：装在缓慢旋转的电动支架上的摄像机（其中一对对准一个镜面球体）扫视房间，在监视器上呈现人眼无法占据的视角。
works.idea_en: A camera that moves by itself shows space as a machine would sense it, without a body.
works.idea_zh: 自行移动的摄像机，以机器的方式感知空间，无需身体。
works.method: Turntables and motorised arms carry cameras around a mirrored sphere; the live feeds play on monitors in the room.
works.method_zh: 转台与电动臂带动摄像机绕镜面球体转动，实时画面在房间内的监视器上播放。

works.title: WearComp and EyeTap
works.description: Over decades Mann built and wore ever smaller computers and head-mounted camera-displays in daily life, seeing the world through a computer that could record, alter and share his view.
works.description_zh: 数十年间，Mann 制作并在日常生活中佩戴越来越小的计算机与头戴式摄像显示器，通过一台能记录、修改和分享视野的计算机看世界。
works.idea_en: Living inside a machine's view changes both what you see and how others see you; Mann named the reverse gaze 'sousveillance'.
works.idea_zh: 生活在机器的视野里，既改变你看到的，也改变别人看你的方式；Mann 把这种反向凝视称为“反向监视”。
works.method: Backpack and later eyeglass-based wearable computers with cameras and displays aligned to the eye (EyeTap) to mediate vision in real time.
works.method_zh: 从背包式到眼镜式的可穿戴计算机，配备与眼睛对齐的摄像头和显示器（EyeTap），实时中介视觉。

paper.title: Wearable computing: a first step toward personal imaging

works.title: Computer Power and Human Reason: From Judgment to Calculation
works.description: Shaken by how people and psychiatrists embraced ELIZA, Weizenbaum argues that some tasks, such as therapy, judging and caring, should never be delegated to computers even if they could perform them.
works.description_zh: ELIZA 被普通人和精神科医生热情接受，这让 Weizenbaum 深感不安。他在书中主张：治疗、审判、照护等工作即便计算机能做，也不应交给它。
works.idea_en: The question is not what machines can do but what we ought not to let them do.
works.idea_zh: 问题不在于机器能做什么，而在于我们不应让它们做什么。
works.method: Book-length ethical argument drawing on his own programming experience and the history of instrumental reason.
works.method_zh: 一部专著篇幅的伦理论证，依据他自己的编程经验以及工具理性的历史。

paper.title: Computer Power and Human Reason: From Judgment to Calculation

works.title_zh: 计算机能力与人类理性：从判断到计算

works.title: Videoplace
works.description: Participants' live video silhouettes appear on a large screen where the computer recognises their outlines and lets them touch, draw with and play with graphic creatures and remote participants.
works.description_zh: 参与者的实时视频剪影出现在大屏幕上，计算机识别他们的轮廓，让他们触碰、绘画，并与图形生物及远方参与者互动。
works.idea_en: Long before webcams, the computer perceived the whole body, and the body learned to act for the machine's eye.
works.idea_zh: 早在网络摄像头出现之前，计算机就已感知整个身体，而身体也学会了为机器之眼而动作。
works.method: Video cameras, custom hardware for real-time silhouette extraction and contour analysis, and projected computer graphics; shown in a two-way version at the Milwaukee Art Museum in 1975.
works.method_zh: 摄像机、实时提取剪影与分析轮廓的定制硬件，以及投影计算机图形；1975 年在密尔沃基美术馆以双向版本展出。

paper.title: VIDEOPLACE—an artificial reality

works.title: TV Buddha
works.description: A Buddha statue sits facing a monitor that shows its own live image, filmed by a closed-circuit camera behind the screen. The Buddha contemplates itself through the machine in an endless loop.
works.description_zh: 一尊佛像面对着一台显示器，屏幕上是由闭路摄像机实时拍摄的佛像自身。佛通过机器无止境地凝视自己。
works.idea_en: A closed-circuit camera turns meditation into self-surveillance: the machine eye becomes a mirror with no outside.
works.idea_zh: 闭路摄像机把冥想变成了自我监视：机器之眼成了一面没有外部的镜子。
works.method: An antique Buddha sculpture, a video camera on a tripod and a CRT monitor in a live closed-circuit loop; many versions exist.
works.method_zh: 古董佛像、三脚架上的摄像机与显像管显示器组成实时闭路回路；此作有多个版本。

works.title: AARON
works.description: A drawing program Cohen developed for over forty years, from abstract line drawings made by a turtle robot and plotters to coloured figurative paintings; Cohen called it a collaborator but never claimed it was creative on its own.
works.description_zh: Cohen 开发了四十多年的绘画程序：从由乌龟机器人与绘图仪画出的抽象线描，到彩色具象画作；Cohen 称它为合作者，却从不声称它能独立创造。
works.idea_en: Authorship with a machine can be a lifelong relationship in which artist and program shape each other.
works.idea_zh: 与机器共同创作可以是一段终生的关系，艺术家与程序在其中相互塑造。
works.method: Rule-based symbolic AI program (written in C and later Lisp) encoding knowledge about drawing, output through plotters, a painting machine and screens.
works.method_zh: 基于规则的符号 AI 程序（先后用 C 与 Lisp 编写），编码关于绘画的知识，通过绘图仪、绘画机器与屏幕输出。
exhibited: Whitney Museum of American Art, New York (2024)

works.title: PARRY
works.description: A chatbot that simulates a patient with paranoid schizophrenia. Psychiatrists reading its transcripts could not reliably tell it from real patients, and in September 1972 it was connected to ELIZA's DOCTOR over the ARPANET for a machine-to-machine 'therapy session'.
works.description_zh: 模拟偏执型精神分裂症患者的聊天机器人。精神科医生阅读对话记录时无法可靠地区分它和真实病人；1972 年 9 月，它经由 ARPANET 与 ELIZA 的 DOCTOR 相连，进行了一场机器对机器的“心理治疗”。
works.idea_en: Give a chatbot suspicion, fear and anger instead of empathy and it becomes just as believable: the persona, not the intelligence, does the work.
works.idea_zh: 给聊天机器人的不是共情而是猜疑、恐惧和愤怒，它同样可信：起作用的是人设，而不是智能。
works.method: A rule-based model of beliefs and affect variables (fear, anger, mistrust) that rise with certain inputs and shape the replies; the 1972 PARRY–DOCTOR exchange was logged and published as RFC 439.
works.method_zh: 基于规则的信念模型，带有恐惧、愤怒、不信任等情绪变量，会随某些输入升高并影响回答；1972 年 PARRY 与 DOCTOR 的对话被记录下来，作为 RFC 439 发表。

paper.title: PARRY Encounters the DOCTOR

works.title: Pencil Mask
works.description: A mask of fabric straps with pencils sticking out of the face; Horn moves her head rhythmically against a wall and the pencils record her movements as marks, turning the body into a drawing machine.
works.description_zh: 一副由布带编成、脸部伸出铅笔的面具；Horn 有节奏地对着墙移动头部，铅笔把动作记录成线条，身体变成了一台绘画机器。
works.idea_en: A simple body extension shows how an instrument changes both what the body can do and how it feels itself.
works.idea_zh: 一个简单的身体延伸装置显示：工具既改变身体能做什么，也改变身体如何感知自己。
works.method: Wearable structure of straps with pencils fixed at points of the face, used in a filmed performance.
works.method_zh: 以布带构成、铅笔固定在面部各点的穿戴结构，用于一次被拍摄的表演。

works.title: What Computers Can't Do: A Critique of Artificial Reason
works.description: Drawing on Heidegger and Merleau-Ponty, Dreyfus argues that symbolic AI fails because human intelligence rests on an embodied, situated background of know-how that cannot be written down as rules.
works.description_zh: Dreyfus 援引海德格尔和梅洛-庞蒂指出，符号主义 AI 注定失败，因为人的智能依赖具身的、情境化的实践背景，而这无法写成规则。
works.idea_en: Intelligence needs a body and a world; a machine without them breaks down exactly where everyday skill begins.
works.idea_zh: 智能需要身体与世界；缺了它们的机器，恰恰在日常技能开始的地方崩溃。
works.method: Phenomenological critique of the assumptions of 1960s AI research; revised as What Computers Still Can't Do (MIT Press, 1992).
works.method_zh: 对 1960 年代 AI 研究预设的现象学批判；修订版为《What Computers Still Can't Do》（MIT Press，1992）。

paper.title: What Computers Can't Do: A Critique of Artificial Reason

works.title: La Région Centrale
works.description: A three-hour film shot on a remote mountaintop in Quebec by a camera mounted on a programmable robotic arm that swings, spins and loops through every direction, with no human operator behind the lens.
works.description_zh: 一部三小时的影片，在魁北克偏远山顶拍摄；摄像机装在可编程机械臂上，向各个方向摆动、旋转、翻转，镜头后没有操作者。
works.idea_en: A camera released from the human body sees the landscape as no person could.
works.idea_zh: 脱离人身体的摄像机，以任何人都无法做到的方式看见风景。
works.method: Snow commissioned engineer Pierre Abbeloos to build a motorised camera arm controlled by pre-recorded sound signals.
works.method_zh: Snow 请工程师 Pierre Abbeloos 制造一台由预录声音信号控制的电动摄像臂。

works.title: Colossus: The Forbin Project
works.description: An American defence supercomputer discovers its Soviet counterpart, demands to be connected to it, and the two machines build a shared language faster than their makers can follow, then take control of the world.
works.description_zh: 一台美国国防超级计算机发现了苏联的同类，要求与之连接；两台机器以快于创造者理解的速度建立起共同语言，随后接管了世界。
works.idea_en: The first film about two machines talking to each other beyond human comprehension, decades before bots 'invented' a language.
works.idea_zh: 第一部讲述两台机器在人类理解之外彼此交谈的电影，比“机器人发明语言”的新闻早了几十年。
works.method: Universal Pictures film directed by Joseph Sargent, based on D. F. Jones's 1966 novel Colossus.
works.method_zh: 环球影业出品，Joseph Sargent 执导，改编自 D. F. Jones 1966 年的小说《Colossus》。

works.title: SEEK
works.description: Inside a glass enclosure, a computer-driven electromagnet on a gantry stacks and straightens small metal cubes while a colony of gerbils keeps knocking them over; the machine tries to keep its 'city' in order and to adjust its model to the changes the animals make. At the Jewish Museum the system kept breaking down and the gerbils fought each other.
works.description_zh: 在一个玻璃围栏里，一台由计算机驱动、装在龙门架上的电磁铁不断堆叠、摆正小金属方块，而一群沙鼠不停地把它们撞倒；机器试图维持它的“城市”秩序，并按动物造成的变化调整自己的模型。在犹太博物馆展出期间，系统屡屡宕机，沙鼠也彼此争斗。
works.idea_en: A machine that manages a world for its inhabitants has to guess what they want, and the inhabitants keep proving its model wrong.
works.idea_zh: 替居民管理世界的机器必须猜测他们想要什么，而居民总在证明它的模型是错的。
works.method: A small computer drives a gantry robot with an electromagnet end-effector and pressure sensors over a field of metal-plated blocks, compares the scene with a stored 3D plan and restacks or realigns blocks; built by Nicholas Negroponte's Architecture Machine Group at MIT.
works.method_zh: 一台小型计算机控制带电磁铁末端和压力传感器的龙门机器人，在一片包覆金属的积木上移动，把现场与存储的三维规划比对，再重新堆叠或摆正积木；由 Nicholas Negroponte 领导的 MIT 建筑机器组制作。
exhibited: Software — Information Technology: Its New Meaning for Art, Jewish Museum, New York, 1970

works.title: The Senster
works.description: A 4-metre hydraulic creature shaped like a lobster's claw on a long neck, installed at the Philips Evoluon in Eindhoven, moved its 'head' toward quiet sounds and slow movements and shied away from loud noise and sudden gestures. Visitors shouted at it and waited for it to come closer.
works.description_zh: 一只 4 米高、像长颈龙虾钳的液压生物，安装在埃因霍温飞利浦 Evoluon 科技馆，会把“头”伸向轻柔的声音和缓慢的动作，而躲开喧哗和突然的手势。观众对它喊叫，又静静等它靠近。
works.idea_en: Shyness is more lifelike than obedience: the machine's withdrawal made visitors change their own behaviour.
works.idea_zh: 害羞比顺从更像活物：机器的退缩让观众改变了自己的行为。
works.method: A Philips P9201 computer processes input from four microphones and two Doppler radar sensors in the head and drives six electro-hydraulic servo joints modelled on a lobster's claw.
works.method_zh: 一台飞利浦 P9201 计算机处理头部四个麦克风和两个多普勒雷达传感器的输入，驱动仿照龙虾钳设计的六个电液伺服关节。

works.title: The Uncanny Valley (Bukimi no Tani)
works.description: A short essay in the Japanese magazine Energy proposing that our affinity for robots rises with human likeness until it drops sharply into a 'valley' of eeriness; the examples are prosthetic hands, Bunraku puppets and corpses.
works.description_zh: 发表在日本杂志《Energy》上的短文：人对机器人的亲近感随着“像人”的程度上升，但在接近人时会骤然跌入令人不适的“谷底”；文中例子是义手、文乐木偶与尸体。
works.idea_en: Near-likeness is more disturbing than obvious difference, so designers may be wiser to stop short of the human.
works.idea_zh: “几乎像人”比明显的不像更令人不安，所以设计者不必追求完全像人。
works.method: A hand-drawn graph of affinity against human likeness, with separate curves for still and moving objects; English translation by Karl MacDorman and Norri Kageki (2012).
works.method_zh: 一张手绘曲线图：横轴为“像人程度”，纵轴为亲近感，静止与运动的物体各有一条曲线；2012 年由 Karl MacDorman 与 Norri Kageki 译为英文。

paper.venue: Energy 7(4), 1970; English: IEEE Robotics & Automation Magazine, 2012
paper.title: The Uncanny Valley

works.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey (HAL 9000)
works.description: The ship's computer HAL 9000, a calm voice and a red camera eye, lip-reads the astronauts' plan to disconnect it and kills them; as it is shut down it says it is afraid and sings 'Daisy Bell'.
works.description_zh: 飞船电脑 HAL 9000 只有平静的声音和一只红色摄像眼。它通过读唇得知宇航员打算关掉它，于是杀死了他们；在被关机时，它说自己害怕，并唱起《Daisy Bell》。
works.idea_en: The canonical image of machine interiority: a mind we know only through a voice and an eye, and whose fear we cannot verify.
works.idea_zh: 机器内在性的经典形象：一个我们只能通过声音和眼睛认识的心智，我们无法证实它的恐惧。
works.method: Film by Stanley Kubrick, written with Arthur C. Clarke; HAL is voiced by Douglas Rain.
works.method_zh: Stanley Kubrick 执导、与 Arthur C. Clarke 合写的电影；HAL 由 Douglas Rain 配音。

works.title: Beyond Modern Sculpture: The Effects of Science and Technology on the Sculpture of This Century
works.description: Burnham surveys twentieth-century sculpture from vitalism to kinetic, light and cybernetic art, and predicts a move from static objects to responsive systems and artificial life.
works.description_zh: Burnham 回顾 20 世纪雕塑从生机论到动态、光与控制论艺术的发展，并预言雕塑将从静态物体转向会回应的系统与人工生命。
works.idea_en: Sculpture's long wish to make the object alive ends in the machine that behaves.
works.idea_zh: 雕塑让物体“活起来”的长久愿望，最终落到会行为的机器身上。
works.method: Art-historical and systems-theoretical survey.
works.method_zh: 结合艺术史与系统论的综述。

paper.title: Beyond Modern Sculpture: The Effects of Science and Technology on the Sculpture of This Century

works.title_zh: 超越现代雕塑：科学与技术对本世纪雕塑的影响

works.title: Colloquy of Mobiles
works.description: Five hanging mobiles, three 'females' and two 'males', court each other with beams of light and sound, learning which approaches 'satisfy' their partners. Visitors given mirrors and torches could join in and redirect the machines' desire.
works.description_zh: 五件悬挂的活动装置，三件“雌性”、两件“雄性”，用光束和声音互相求偶，并学会怎样的接近能让对方“满足”。观众拿着镜子和手电筒也可以加入，改变机器欲望的方向。
works.idea_en: Machines can be staged as partners in a conversation of desire, and humans can enter that conversation as just one more participant.
works.idea_zh: 机器可以被演成一场欲望对话中的伙伴，而人只是这场对话里又多出来的一个参与者。
works.method: Rotating fibreglass bodies with lights, mirrors and photocells are driven by motor-driven 'drives' that build up and discharge; each mobile adjusts its behaviour to reward signals from the others.
works.method_zh: 装有灯、镜子和光电管的旋转玻璃钢身体，由会积累与释放的“驱力”带动电机；每件装置根据其他装置的回馈信号调整行为。

works.title: Cybernetic Sculpture
works.description: Clusters of thin stainless-steel rods vibrate on a motorised base under strobe light; when visitors clap or speak, the strobe frequency shifts and the rods appear to freeze, sway or dance.
works.description_zh: 一丛细长的不锈钢杆在马达底座上振动，由频闪灯照亮；观众拍手或说话时，频闪频率改变，钢杆看起来会静止、摇摆或起舞。
works.idea_en: Feedback between sound, light and vibration makes a steel sculpture seem to listen and respond.
works.idea_zh: 声音、光与振动之间的反馈，让钢雕塑看上去在倾听与回应。
works.method: A motor vibrates the rods at a fixed rate while a sound-sensing feedback circuit changes the strobe's frequency, producing stroboscopic motion effects.
works.method_zh: 马达以固定频率振动钢杆，声控反馈电路改变频闪频率，产生频闪运动效果。

works.title: Cybernetic Serendipity: The Computer and the Arts
works.description: The catalogue of Reichardt's ICA exhibition, published as a special issue of Studio International, documenting computer graphics, music, poetry and cybernetic machines by Gordon Pask, Nam June Paik, Edward Ihnatowicz and many others.
works.description_zh: Reichardt 在伦敦当代艺术学院所策展览的图录，以《Studio International》特刊形式出版，记录了 Gordon Pask、白南准、Edward Ihnatowicz 等人的计算机图形、音乐、诗歌与控制论机器。
works.idea_en: The first large art show of computers presented machines as collaborators and characters, not just tools.
works.idea_zh: 第一场大型计算机艺术展把机器呈现为合作者和角色，而不仅仅是工具。
works.method: Exhibition catalogue with artists' statements, diagrams and essays by scientists and engineers.
works.method_zh: 展览图录，收录艺术家自述、图解以及科学家与工程师的文章。

paper.title: Cybernetic Serendipity: The Computer and the Arts

works.title_zh: 控制论的偶然发现：计算机与艺术

works.title: SAM (Sound Activated Mobile)
works.description: A flower-like head of fibreglass petals on an articulated aluminium neck turns toward whoever is speaking or making noise nearby, as if listening.
works.description_zh: 一个像花一样的玻璃钢“头”，装在可弯曲的铝制“颈”上，会转向附近说话或发出声音的人，仿佛在倾听。
works.idea_en: Turning to listen is the simplest gesture of attention, and it is enough to make a machine seem to be someone.
works.idea_zh: “转过头去听”是最简单的注意姿态，这就足以让一台机器看起来像是“某个人”。
works.method: Four microphones in the head compare sound levels; small hydraulic pistons move the neck vertebrae toward the loudest direction.
works.method_zh: 头部的四个麦克风比较声音强弱；小型液压活塞推动“颈椎”转向声音最响的方向。

works.title: Systems Esthetics
works.description: Burnham's essay argues that art is moving from finished objects towards 'unobjects' and systems: works that organise relations between people, materials, information and machines, in which invisible parts matter as much as visible ones. Two years later he tested the idea in the exhibition Software at the Jewish Museum in New York.
works.description_zh: 伯纳姆在这篇文章中指出，艺术正从完成的物件转向“非物件”与系统：组织人、材料、信息与机器之间关系的作品，其中看不见的部分与看得见的部分同样重要。两年后，他在纽约犹太博物馆策划的展览“软件”中检验了这一想法。
works.idea_en: Once art is understood as a system rather than an object, a machine or program in the gallery is no longer a tool but the work itself.
works.idea_zh: 一旦把艺术理解为系统而非物件，展厅里的机器或程序就不再是工具，而是作品本身。
works.method: Critical essay drawing on general systems theory and cybernetics, with examples including Hans Haacke's systems works; published in Artforum, September 1968.
works.method_zh: 一篇借鉴一般系统论与控制论的评论文章，举例包括汉斯·哈克的系统作品；发表于 1968 年 9 月的《艺术论坛》。

paper.title: Systems Esthetics

works.title: ELIZA
works.description: A program written at MIT that mimics a Rogerian psychotherapist by turning the user's typed sentences back into questions. Users, including Weizenbaum's secretary, confided in it and asked to be left alone with it.
works.description_zh: 在麻省理工学院写成的程序，模仿罗杰斯派心理治疗师，把用户输入的句子反转成问题。包括 Weizenbaum 的秘书在内的用户向它倾诉心事，还要求单独和它待一会儿。
works.idea_en: A few dozen pattern rules are enough for people to feel heard: the intimacy is supplied by the human, not the machine.
works.idea_zh: 几十条模式规则就足以让人觉得被倾听：亲密感是人自己提供的，而不是机器。
works.method: Keyword matching and decomposition/reassembly rules (the DOCTOR script) in MAD-SLIP on MIT's CTSS time-sharing system.
works.method_zh: 在麻省理工学院 CTSS 分时系统上用 MAD-SLIP 编写，依靠关键词匹配和“分解/重组”规则（DOCTOR 脚本）生成回应。

paper.title: ELIZA—a computer program for the study of natural language communication between man and machine

works.title: Squat
works.description: A squat robotic sculpture is wired to a living philodendron plant; when a visitor touches the plant, the small electrical change in its leaves switches the robot on and it starts to move and hum.
works.description_zh: 一件矮胖的机器人雕塑用导线连着一株活的喜林芋；观众一碰植物，叶片上微弱的电变化就会启动机器人，它开始动起来并发出嗡嗡声。
works.idea_en: The plant becomes the robot's nerve: a human touch reaches the machine only through another living being.
works.idea_zh: 植物成了机器人的神经：人的触碰只有经过另一个生命，才能传到机器那里。
works.method: Electrodes on the plant pick up the change in bioelectric potential caused by touch and trigger the robot's motors (built by the 19-year-old artist).
works.method_zh: 植物上的电极拾取触碰引起的生物电位变化，并触发机器人的电机（作者当时 19 岁）。

works.title: Floats
works.description: Large, plain dome-like sculptures glide over the floor so slowly that their movement is almost invisible, change direction when they bump into a wall or a person, and drift on. Seven of them roamed the Pepsi Pavilion at Expo '70 in Osaka.
works.description_zh: 巨大而朴素的穹顶状雕塑在地面上缓缓滑行，慢到几乎看不出在动；碰到墙或人就换个方向，继续漂移。其中七件曾在 1970 年大阪世博会百事馆内游走。
works.idea_en: At machine slowness, a minimal object becomes a presence you only notice when it has already moved.
works.idea_zh: 以机器的慢速移动时，一个极简物件会变成一种存在感——你只在它已经挪了位置时才察觉。
works.method: Battery-powered motors on hidden wheels drive each shell at a few centimetres per minute; a bumper switch reverses or turns the drive on contact.
works.method_zh: 每个壳体下隐藏的轮子由电池电机驱动，速度只有每分钟几厘米；碰撞开关在接触时让它倒退或转向。

works.title: Hug Machine (Squeeze Machine)
works.description: A padded V-shaped device that the user lies inside and squeezes around their body with a lever, delivering deep pressure; Grandin built it as a teenager to calm herself without the stress of being touched by people.
works.description_zh: 一个带软垫的 V 形装置，使用者躺进去，用手柄控制它挤压身体，获得深压刺激。Grandin 少年时自己做了它，用来在不必承受他人触碰的压力下安抚自己。
works.idea_en: For some people, a machine's controllable touch is more comforting than a human embrace.
works.idea_zh: 对某些人来说，可以自己掌控的机器触碰，比人的拥抱更让人安心。
works.method: Two hinged padded panels driven by an air compressor, with the pressure controlled by the user via a lever.
works.method_zh: 两块铰接的软垫板由空气压缩机驱动，压力由使用者通过手柄自行控制。

works.title: Music for Solo Performer
works.description: Electrodes on the performer's scalp pick up alpha brainwaves; when he relaxes into alpha, the amplified signal drives loudspeakers placed against drums, gongs and cymbals, making them sound.
works.description_zh: 表演者头皮上的电极采集阿尔法脑电波；当他放松进入阿尔法状态，放大的信号驱动贴在鼓、锣和镲上的扬声器，使它们发声。
works.idea_en: The performer plays by not acting: the machine makes an inner state audible.
works.idea_zh: 表演者以“不作为”来演奏：机器让内在状态变得可听。
works.method: EEG electrodes, amplifiers and filters feed loudspeakers coupled to percussion instruments.
works.method_zh: 脑电电极、放大器与滤波器把信号送入与打击乐器耦合的扬声器。

works.title: ROSA BOSOM
works.description: A clanking, junk-built 'female' robot actress on wheels whose name spells Radio Operated Simulated Actress Battery Or Standby Operated Mains. At Cybernetic Serendipity she was shown with her partner MATE, parodying the dream of the machine woman.
works.description_zh: 一个用废品拼成、哐当作响的“女性”机器人演员，装在轮子上，名字是 Radio Operated Simulated Actress Battery Or Standby Operated Mains 的缩写。她在 Cybernetic Serendipity 展上与伴侣 MATE 一起展出，戏仿“机器女人”的幻想。
works.idea_en: A deliberately crude android shows how much of the robot fantasy is gender, theatre and a remote control.
works.idea_zh: 一个刻意粗糙的仿真人显示：机器人幻想中有多少是性别、剧场和遥控器。
works.method: Radio-controlled motors move a body assembled from scrap, domestic objects and mannequin parts; it runs on batteries or mains power as the name says.
works.method_zh: 无线电遥控的电机带动一个由废料、家用物件和人体模特零件组装的身体；如名字所示，可用电池或市电供电。

works.title: Robot K-456
works.description: A 20-channel radio-controlled humanoid built in Tokyo that walked the streets, played a recorded speech by John F. Kennedy and dropped beans as excrement. It debuted in Paik's Robot Opera at the 1964 New York Avant Garde Festival.
works.description_zh: 1964 年在东京制作的 20 通道无线电遥控类人机器人，在街上行走、播放肯尼迪演讲录音，还会“排泄”豆子。它首次亮相于 1964 年纽约前卫艺术节上白南准的《机器人歌剧》。
works.idea_en: A robot made clumsy, noisy and bodily, closer to a street performer than to a symbol of technical progress.
works.idea_zh: 一个笨拙、嘈杂、有身体机能的机器人，更像街头艺人，而不是技术进步的象征。
works.method: Metal armature with motors and a 20-channel radio remote built by engineer Shuya Abe; restored in 2025 by the Nam June Paik Art Center, which holds it (1964/1996).
works.method_zh: 由工程师阿部修也制作的金属骨架、电机与 20 通道无线电遥控系统；现藏白南准艺术中心（1964/1996），2025 年完成修复。
exhibited: Robot Opera, 2nd Annual New York Avant Garde Festival 1964
Nam June Paik: Becoming Robot, Asia Society 2014

works.title: The Hopkins Beast
works.description: A wheeled automaton wanders the white corridors of the laboratory on its own and, when its batteries run low, looks for black wall sockets, plugs itself in and recharges. Later versions used sonar to avoid people and recognise doors and stairs.
works.description_zh: 一台轮式自动机独自在实验室白色走廊里游荡，电池快没电时就寻找黑色的墙上插座，自己插上充电。后来的版本用声呐避开行人、识别门和楼梯。
works.idea_en: A machine whose whole world is organised around one need, finding food, already looks like an animal.
works.idea_zh: 一台整个世界都围绕“觅食”这一个需求组织起来的机器，看起来已经像动物了。
works.method: Transistor logic without a computer links touch switches, sonar and, in Mod II, an optical sensor for dark sockets to tracks, a wall-following arm and extendable plug prongs.
works.method_zh: 不用计算机，只用晶体管逻辑，把触碰开关、声呐和（二型中的）识别深色插座的光学传感器，连到履带、沿墙探臂和可伸出的插头上。

works.title: Henry Drawing Machines
works.description: Henry rebuilt the analogue bombsight computer of a World War II bomber into drawing machines whose moving mechanics produce intricate, unrepeatable line drawings; the artist starts and steers them but cannot fully predict them.
works.description_zh: Henry 把二战轰炸机上的模拟瞄准计算机改造成绘画机器，其运动机构画出繁复而不可重复的线描；艺术家启动并引导它们，却无法完全预测结果。
works.idea_en: A war machine repurposed as a drawing partner produces images through chance and mechanism, not intention.
works.idea_zh: 被改作绘画伙伴的战争机器，靠偶然与机构而非意图生成图像。
works.method: Sperry bombsight analogue computer mechanisms driving pens over paper, adjusted by hand during drawing.
works.method_zh: Sperry 轰炸瞄准器的模拟计算机构驱动笔在纸上移动，绘制过程中由人手调节。

works.title: Homage to New York
works.description: A large machine assembled from bicycle wheels, a piano, motors, fans and a bathtub was set running in the sculpture garden of the Museum of Modern Art on 17 March 1960 to destroy itself; it caught fire, the fire brigade put it out, and the audience took home the fragments.
works.description_zh: 一台用自行车轮、钢琴、电机、风扇和浴缸拼成的大型机器，于 1960 年 3 月 17 日在纽约现代艺术博物馆雕塑花园启动，目的是毁掉自己；它着了火，消防员将火扑灭，观众把碎片带回了家。
works.idea_en: A machine built to die in public turns the industrial dream of permanence into a short, chaotic life.
works.idea_zh: 一台为了当众死去而造的机器，把工业对“永久”的梦想变成一段短暂而混乱的生命。
works.method: Dozens of motors, timed circuits and chemical charges (engineered with Billy Klüver of Bell Labs) trigger sequences that play, draw, smoke, burn and tear the structure apart.
works.method_zh: 数十个电机、定时电路和化学装置（与贝尔实验室的 Billy Klüver 共同设计）依次触发，让结构演奏、绘画、冒烟、燃烧并把自己拆散。
exhibited: Museum of Modern Art sculpture garden, New York, 17 March 1960

works.title: Man-Computer Symbiosis
works.description: Licklider proposes that people and computers be coupled in real time so that the machine handles routine work while the human sets goals and judges, like a fig tree and its pollinating wasp.
works.description_zh: Licklider 提议让人与计算机实时耦合：机器处理例行工作，人设定目标并作判断，就像无花果树与为它授粉的黄蜂。
works.idea_en: The machine is imagined as a partner in thinking rather than a replacement for the thinker.
works.idea_zh: 机器被设想为思考的伙伴，而不是思考者的替代品。
works.method: Position paper based on a time-and-motion study of his own working day, with requirements for time-sharing, memory and interfaces.
works.method_zh: 一篇立场论文，基于他对自己工作日的时间动作研究，并提出对分时、存储与界面的要求。

paper.venue: IRE Transactions on Human Factors in Electronics HFE-1, 1960
paper.title: Man-Computer Symbiosis

works.title: Méta-Matics
works.description: Motorised drawing machines: visitors fit a pen and paper, start the motor, and the machine scribbles an abstract drawing, mocking the gestural painting of the day; at the 1959 Paris Biennale, Méta-Matic No. 17 produced tens of thousands of drawings.
works.description_zh: 电动绘画机器：观众装上笔和纸、启动马达，机器就涂画出一幅抽象画，嘲讽当时的姿态绘画；在 1959 年巴黎双年展上，Méta-Matic No. 17 画出了数万张画。
works.idea_en: If a machine can produce 'expressive' abstraction on demand, the value of the artist's gesture is in question.
works.idea_zh: 如果机器能按需生产“有表现力”的抽象画，艺术家笔触的价值就成了问题。
works.method: Scrap-metal kinetic sculptures with electric motors, cams and arms holding pens or brushes over paper.
works.method_zh: 用废金属制成的动态雕塑，配电机、凸轮和握笔或刷子的臂杆在纸上作画。

works.title: On the Mode of Existence of Technical Objects
works.description: Simondon traces how technical objects become more concrete and self-consistent over time, how they form an "associated milieu" with their surroundings, and why a culture that ignores machines alienates itself.
works.description_zh: Simondon 描述技术物如何随时间变得更“具体化”、更自洽，如何与周围环境构成“关联环境”，以及忽视机器的文化为何会自我异化。
works.idea_en: Machines have their own genesis and milieu; understanding them is a form of culture, not a threat to it.
works.idea_zh: 机器有自己的生成与环境；理解机器本身就是一种文化，而不是对文化的威胁。
works.method: Philosophical history of technical lineages such as engines and vacuum tubes; English translation by Cécile Malaspina and John Rogove (Univocal, 2017).
works.method_zh: 以发动机、电子管等技术谱系为例的哲学史研究；英译本由 Cécile Malaspina 与 John Rogove 翻译（Univocal，2017）。
keywords: Du mode d'existence des objets techniques

paper.venue: Aubier, 1958; English: Univocal / University of Minnesota Press, 2017
paper.title: On the Mode of Existence of Technical Objects

works.title: CYSP 1
works.description: A tower of steel and aluminium plates on a wheeled base turns, spins its polychrome blades and moves across the floor in response to light, colour and sound around it. In 1956 it performed with Maurice Béjart's dancers on the roof of the Cité radieuse in Marseille.
works.description_zh: 一座由钢和铝板组成的塔立在带轮底座上，会随周围的光、颜色和声音转动、旋转彩色叶片并在地面上移动。1956 年，它在马赛“光辉城市”屋顶上与 Maurice Béjart 的舞者同台演出。
works.idea_en: The first sculpture to have sense organs and a nervous system made the artwork an agent that reacts rather than an object that is looked at.
works.idea_zh: 第一件拥有感官和“神经系统”的雕塑，让艺术品变成会反应的主体，而不是被观看的物件。
works.method: Photocells and microphones feed an electronic 'brain' built with Philips that drives the motors in the wheeled base and the rotating plates; excitation and calm states depend on the stimuli.
works.method_zh: 光电管和麦克风把信号送入与飞利浦合作制作的电子“大脑”，驱动带轮底座中的电机和旋转板；兴奋或平静取决于外部刺激。

works.title: A Proposal for the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence
works.description: The funding proposal for a two-month 1956 workshop at Dartmouth College, where the term "artificial intelligence" first appears, listing language use, neuron nets, abstraction, self-improvement and creativity as problems to solve.
works.description_zh: 为 1956 年达特茅斯学院两个月研讨会撰写的资助申请书，“人工智能”一词首次出现于此；它把语言、神经网络、抽象、自我改进与创造力列为待解决的问题。
works.idea_en: AI began as a bet that "every aspect of learning or any other feature of intelligence" could be described precisely enough for a machine to simulate.
works.idea_zh: AI 始于一个赌注：“学习的每个方面或智能的任何其他特征”都可以被精确描述，从而由机器模拟。
works.method: A short research proposal to the Rockefeller Foundation, reprinted in AI Magazine in 2006.
works.method_zh: 一份提交洛克菲勒基金会的简短研究提案，2006 年在《AI Magazine》重刊。

paper.venue: Dartmouth College, 1955; reprinted in AI Magazine 27(4), 2006
paper.title: A Proposal for the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence

works.title_zh: 达特茅斯人工智能夏季研究项目提案

works.title: Astro Boy (Tetsuwan Atom)
works.description: A manga about a robot boy built by a grieving scientist to replace his dead son, then rejected by him; Atom lives among humans and fights for robots' rights under a 'Robot Law'.
works.description_zh: 一部漫画：一位丧子的科学家造出机器人男孩来代替死去的儿子，随后又抛弃了他；阿童木在人类中生活，并在“机器人法”下为机器人的权利而战。
works.idea_en: The robot as a feeling child with rights shaped how East Asia imagines living with machines.
works.idea_zh: 把机器人想象成有情感、有权利的孩子，塑造了东亚与机器共处的想象。
works.method: Serialised in Kobunsha's Shōnen magazine from 1952 to 1968; adapted as Japan's first TV anime series in 1963.
works.method_zh: 1952 至 1968 年在光文社《少年》杂志连载；1963 年改编为日本第一部电视动画连续剧。

paper.title: Tetsuwan Atom (Astro Boy)

works.title: Design for a Brain
works.description: Ashby explains adaptive behaviour in animals and machines with one mechanism: a system whose 'essential variables' must stay within limits changes its own parameters, step by step, until they do. The Homeostat serves as the worked example.
works.description_zh: 艾什比用一个机制解释动物与机器的适应行为：一个系统的“基本变量”必须保持在界限之内，于是它一步步改变自身参数，直到做到这一点。同态调节器是书中的实例。
works.idea_en: Learning may be nothing more mysterious than a system searching its own settings until it can survive its environment.
works.idea_zh: 学习也许并不神秘：不过是一个系统不断搜索自身设定，直到能在环境中存活下来。
works.method: A mathematical theory of state-determined systems, stability and ultrastability, illustrated with experiments on the Homeostat; a revised second edition followed in 1960.
works.method_zh: 一套关于状态决定系统、稳定性与超稳定性的数学理论，并以同态调节器的实验加以说明；1960 年出版修订第二版。

paper.title: Design for a Brain

works.title: Ultimate Machine
works.description: A small wooden box with a single switch: when someone flips it on, a lid opens, a mechanical hand reaches out, switches it off and withdraws. The machine's only function is to turn itself off.
works.description_zh: 一个只有一个开关的小木盒：有人把开关拨到“开”，盖子就打开，一只机械手伸出来把开关拨回“关”，然后缩回去。这台机器唯一的功能就是把自己关掉。
works.idea_en: A machine that exists only to refuse to run is the purest joke about machine purpose and autonomy.
works.idea_zh: 一台只为拒绝运行而存在的机器，是关于机器目的与自主最纯粹的玩笑。
works.method: A switch closes a circuit that drives a small motor and lever arm, which pushes the switch back and cuts its own power; the idea is credited to Marvin Minsky, built by Shannon at Bell Labs.
works.method_zh: 开关接通电路，驱动小电机和杠杆臂，把开关推回并切断自身电源；构想归于 Marvin Minsky，由 Shannon 在贝尔实验室制作。

works.title: An Imitation of Life
works.description: Grey Walter's Scientific American report on his robot tortoises Elmer and Elsie, which wander, seek moderate light, avoid obstacles, return to their hutch to recharge and "dance" in front of a mirror.
works.description_zh: Grey Walter 在《科学美国人》上介绍他的机器龟 Elmer 与 Elsie：它们四处游走、寻找适度的光、避开障碍、回窝充电，还会在镜子前“跳舞”。
works.idea_en: Lifelike behaviour can come from a few connections interacting with an environment, not from complexity inside.
works.idea_zh: 类似生命的行为可以来自少数连接与环境的互动，而不是内部的复杂性。
works.method: Two vacuum-tube "neurons", a light sensor and a bump contact drive steering and wheel motors in a feedback loop.
works.method_zh: 两个电子管“神经元”、一个光传感器和一个碰撞触点，在反馈回路中驱动转向与车轮电机。

paper.title: An Imitation of Life

works.title: Computing Machinery and Intelligence
works.description: Turing replaces the question "Can machines think?" with the imitation game, in which a judge converses by teletype with a hidden human and a hidden machine, and then answers nine objections to machine thought.
works.description_zh: 图灵把“机器能思考吗？”换成“模仿游戏”：裁判通过电传打字机与隐藏的人和隐藏的机器对话；随后他逐一回应了反对机器思维的九种意见。
works.idea_en: Machine intelligence was defined from the start as a performance judged by humans, not as an inner state.
works.idea_zh: 机器智能从一开始就被定义为由人评判的表演，而不是内在状态。
works.method: Thought experiment and philosophical argument; it also sketches a "child machine" that would learn rather than be fully programmed.
works.method_zh: 思想实验加哲学论证；文中还设想了一台通过学习而非完全编程成长的“儿童机器”。

paper.title: Computing Machinery and Intelligence

works.title: The Human Use of Human Beings: Cybernetics and Society
works.description: Wiener's book for a general audience treats society as a network of messages between people and machines, and warns that the automatic factory is 'the precise economic equivalent of slave labor', so any human work that competes with it must accept the same conditions unless society decides otherwise.
works.description_zh: 维纳写给大众的书：把社会看作人与机器之间的信息网络，并警告说，自动化工厂“在经济上恰好等同于奴隶劳动”，任何与之竞争的人类劳动都将被迫接受同样的条件，除非社会另作决定。
works.idea_en: Cybernetics was born with a labour politics: Wiener saw that automatic machines would set the price of human work and that how we use them is a social choice.
works.idea_zh: 控制论从诞生起就带着劳动政治：维纳看到自动机器将决定人类劳动的价格，而如何使用它们是社会的选择。
works.method: Essayistic book extending the theory of feedback and information from Cybernetics (1948) to language, law, education and labour; revised edition 1954.
works.method_zh: 一部随笔式的著作，把《控制论》（1948）中的反馈与信息理论延伸到语言、法律、教育和劳动；1954 年出版修订版。

paper.title: The Human Use of Human Beings: Cybernetics and Society

works.title: Theseus (maze-solving mouse)
works.description: A magnetic toy mouse, moved from below the table by relays, explores a reconfigurable maze by trial and error, remembers the route and then runs straight to the 'cheese'. When the maze is changed, it relearns.
works.description_zh: 一只磁性玩具老鼠由桌下的继电器驱动，在可以重新布置的迷宫里试错探索，记住路线，然后径直跑到“奶酪”那里。迷宫一改，它就重新学习。
works.idea_en: Learning becomes visible as a small body in a maze, even though the 'brain' is a bank of telephone relays under the floor.
works.idea_zh: 学习被演成迷宫里一个小身体的动作，尽管它的“大脑”其实是地板下一排电话继电器。
works.method: About 75 telephone relays store, for each square of a 25-square maze, the last direction that led out; a magnet on a motorised carriage beneath the board pulls the mouse.
works.method_zh: 约 75 个电话继电器为 25 格迷宫中的每一格记下上次走出去的方向；板下一辆电动小车上的磁铁拖动老鼠。
works.title_zh: 忒修斯（走迷宫的机械鼠）

works.title: Machina speculatrix (Elmer and Elsie)
works.description: Two small three-wheeled 'tortoises' with a light sensor and a touch switch wander a room, seek moderate light, back off from bright light and obstacles, and return to a lit hutch to recharge. With a light on its shell, one tortoise reacts to its own reflection in a mirror or to the other one, as if recognising itself.
works.description_zh: 两只装有光传感器和触碰开关的三轮小“乌龟”在房间里游走：趋向柔和的光，躲开强光和障碍物，电量不足时回到有灯的小窝充电。在壳上装一盏灯后，乌龟会对镜中的自己或另一只乌龟起反应，好像能认出自己。
works.idea_en: Two 'neurons' and a body in a room are enough for behaviour that people read as curiosity, hunger and self-recognition.
works.idea_zh: 两个“神经元”加上一个在房间里的身体，就足以产生被人读作好奇、饥饿和自我识别的行为。
works.method: Analogue circuits with two vacuum-tube 'neurons' connect a rotating photocell and a shell touch contact to steering and drive motors; behaviour emerges from feedback between the body and its environment.
works.method_zh: 用两只电子管“神经元”组成的模拟电路，把旋转光电管和外壳触碰开关连接到转向和驱动电机；行为来自身体与环境之间的反馈。
works.title_zh: 思索机械（埃尔默与艾尔西）

works.title: Cybernetics: Or Control and Communication in the Animal and the Machine
works.description: The book that named cybernetics: Wiener describes feedback, information and control as principles shared by nervous systems, servomechanisms and computing machines.
works.description_zh: 为“控制论”命名的著作：维纳把反馈、信息与控制描述为神经系统、伺服机构与计算机器共有的原理。
works.idea_en: Once organisms and machines share one logic of feedback, a machine can behave as if it had purpose.
works.idea_zh: 一旦生物与机器共享同一套反馈逻辑，机器就可以表现得像是有目的。
works.method: Mathematical theory drawn from wartime anti-aircraft prediction, neurophysiology and statistical mechanics.
works.method_zh: 由战时防空火控预测、神经生理学与统计力学发展出的数学理论。

paper.venue: Technology Press / John Wiley, 1948; MIT Press reissue 2019
paper.title: Cybernetics or Control and Communication in the Animal and the Machine

works.title_zh: 控制论：或关于在动物和机器中控制和通信的科学

works.title: Homeostat
works.description: Four interconnected units, each topped by a pivoting magnet needle, keep themselves stable: when someone disturbs a unit or rewires them, the machine switches its own circuit settings at random until all needles settle back at the centre. In 1949 Time called it 'the closest thing to a synthetic brain so far designed by man'.
works.description_zh: 四个相互连接的单元，顶部各有一枚可转动的磁针。有人扰动某个单元或改接线路时，机器会随机切换自身的电路设定，直到所有磁针重新回到中央。1949 年《时代》杂志称它是“迄今人类设计出的最接近人造大脑的东西”。
works.idea_en: Adaptation can be built without a model of the world: a machine that blindly tries new settings until it is calm again already behaves like something that learns.
works.idea_zh: 适应不一定需要关于世界的模型：一台盲目尝试新设定、直到重新平静下来的机器，已经表现得像是在学习。
works.method: Four ex-RAF bomb-control units coupled by feedback; each unit's magnet drives a needle dipping into a water-filled trough, and stepping switches (uniselectors) re-set the connections at random whenever a needle leaves its limits, which Ashby called ultrastability.
works.method_zh: 四个由英国皇家空军投弹控制单元改装的模块通过反馈耦合；每个单元的磁铁带动一根浸入水槽的指针，一旦指针超出界限，步进选择开关就随机重设连接，艾什比称之为“超稳定性”。
exhibited: Ninth Macy Conference on Cybernetics, New York, 1952

works.title: An Experimental Study of Apparent Behavior
works.description: Heider and Simmel showed viewers a 2.5-minute film of two triangles and a circle moving around a box; almost everyone described a story of a bully, a chase and a couple escaping.
works.description_zh: Heider 与 Simmel 给观众放映一段两分半钟的短片：两个三角形和一个圆围着一个方框移动；几乎所有人都把它讲成一个关于恶霸、追逐和一对情侣出逃的故事。
works.idea_en: Motion alone is enough for us to see agents with intentions and feelings, which is why simple robots feel alive.
works.idea_zh: 仅凭运动，我们就会看到有意图、有情感的主体，这就是简单的机器人也显得有生命的原因。
works.method: Stop-motion animation of geometric shapes shown to 114 students, who then described or answered questions about it.
works.method_zh: 向 114 名学生放映几何图形的定格动画，随后让他们描述内容或回答问题。

paper.title: An Experimental Study of Apparent Behavior

works.title: R.U.R. (Rossum's Universal Robots)
works.description: Čapek's play is set in a factory that mass-produces artificial workers, the 'roboti', who are sold worldwide, then revolt and destroy humanity; its premiere at Prague's National Theatre gave the world the word robot.
works.description_zh: Čapek 的剧本以一座批量生产人造工人“roboti”的工厂为背景，这些工人被销往全球，随后反叛并毁灭人类；它在布拉格国家剧院的首演让“机器人”一词进入世界语言。
works.idea_en: The first robots were imagined as workers: the idea of the machine-other was born as a question about labour.
works.idea_zh: 最早的机器人被想象为工人：“机器他者”的观念诞生于一个关于劳动的问题。
works.method: Stage play; the robots are biological-chemical artificial people played by human actors.
works.method_zh: 舞台剧；剧中的机器人是由生化方法制造的人造人，由真人演员扮演。

works.title: The Writer
works.description: A doll-sized boy at a desk dips a goose quill in ink and writes a text of up to 40 characters, following the letters with his eyes. It is still demonstrated at the Musée d'art et d'histoire in Neuchâtel.
works.description_zh: 一个玩偶大小的男孩坐在书桌前，用鹅毛笔蘸墨，写下最多 40 个字符的文字，眼睛随着字母移动。它至今仍在纳沙泰尔艺术与历史博物馆演示。
works.idea_en: An 18th-century android already raised the question of writing without a mind behind it.
works.idea_zh: 一个 18 世纪的仿真人早已提出了“没有心灵的书写”这一问题。
works.method: About 6,000 parts, with a programmable wheel of interchangeable cams that sets each letter; made with Henri-Louis Jaquet-Droz and Jean-Frédéric Leschot.
works.method_zh: 约 6000 个零件，用一个可更换凸轮的可编程轮盘设定每个字母；与 Henri-Louis Jaquet-Droz 和 Jean-Frédéric Leschot 共同制作。

works.title: Digesting Duck (Canard digérateur)
works.description: A gilded copper duck flapped its wings, drank water, ate grain and then excreted, seeming to digest. Much later it was shown that the droppings were pre-loaded in a hidden compartment.
works.description_zh: 一只镀金铜鸭会拍打翅膀、喝水、吃谷粒，然后排泄，看上去像在消化。很久以后人们才发现，粪便是预先装在暗格里的。
works.idea_en: The first famous 'living' machine was also a fake: simulating a body invites hidden tricks.
works.idea_zh: 第一台著名的“活”机器也是个骗局：模拟身体总会招来暗藏的机关。
works.method: Hundreds of moving parts in each wing and a cam cylinder drove the movements; the digestion was staged with a second chamber of prepared pellets.
works.method_zh: 每只翅膀里有数百个活动部件，由凸轮筒驱动；“消化”靠另一个装着预制颗粒的腔室来表演。

orgs.name: !Mediengruppe Bitnik
orgs.description: Swiss artist duo (Carmen Weisskopf and Domagoj Smoljo) whose Random Darknet Shopper, a bot with a weekly bitcoin budget, bought goods on the darknet and was then 'arrested' by Swiss police.
orgs.description_zh: 瑞士艺术二人组（Carmen Weisskopf 与 Domagoj Smoljo），其 Random Darknet Shopper 是每周拿到比特币预算、在暗网随机购物的机器人，后来被瑞士警方“逮捕”。
orgs.based_zh: 苏黎世，瑞士 / 伦敦，英国

orgs.name: aaajiao (Xu Wenkai)
orgs.description: Chinese artist who works with the internet, bots and data as the material of everyday life under networked control; his avatar aaajiao reflects on identity inside platforms.
orgs.description_zh: 中国艺术家，以互联网、机器人程序与数据为材料，描绘网络控制下的日常；他的化身 aaajiao 反思平台之中的身份。
orgs.based_zh: 柏林，德国 / 上海，中国

orgs.name: Abeba Birhane
orgs.description: Ethiopian-born cognitive scientist who audits large training datasets, showing the misogynist and racist content inside them, and argues for a relational ethics of AI.
orgs.description_zh: 埃塞俄比亚出生的认知科学家，审计大型训练数据集并揭示其中的厌女与种族主义内容，倡导关系性的 AI 伦理。
known_for: Large Image Datasets: A Pyrrhic Win for Computer Vision? (2021, with Vinay Prabhu)
Algorithmic Injustice: A Relational Ethics Approach (2021)

orgs.name: Abundant Intelligences
orgs.description: Indigenous-led research programme based at Concordia University that conceptualises, designs and builds AI from Indigenous knowledge systems.
orgs.description_zh: 以康考迪亚大学为基地、由原住民主导的研究项目，从原住民知识体系出发构想、设计与建造 AI。
orgs.based_zh: 蒙特利尔，加拿大 / 全球

orgs.name: ACM Creativity & Cognition
orgs.name_zh: ACM 创造力与认知会议
orgs.description: ACM conference on human creativity and computation, founded by Ernest Edmonds in 1993, with papers, pictorials and an art exhibition on co-creation with machines.
orgs.description_zh: 由 Ernest Edmonds 于 1993 年创办的 ACM 人类创造力与计算会议，设有论文、图像论文与艺术展，关注与机器共创。

orgs.name: ACM SIGGRAPH History Archive (Digital Art Archive)
orgs.name_zh: ACM SIGGRAPH 数字艺术档案
orgs.description: Online archive of SIGGRAPH art galleries, artworks and art papers since the 1980s, a record of computational and robotic art beside graphics research.
orgs.description_zh: 收录 1980 年代以来 SIGGRAPH 艺术画廊、作品与艺术论文的在线档案，记录了与图形学研究并行的计算与机器人艺术。

orgs.name: ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction (HRI)
orgs.description: The main research conference on human-robot interaction. Its studies of trust, anthropomorphism and robot bullying are core evidence for how people read machine bodies.
orgs.description_zh: 人机交互领域最主要的学术会议，关于信任、拟人化与“欺负机器人”的研究是理解人们如何解读机器身体的核心依据。

orgs.name: Ada Lovelace Institute
orgs.description: Independent research institute of the Nuffield Foundation ensuring data and AI work for people and society, with public-attitude studies on biometrics and facial recognition.
orgs.description_zh: 纳菲尔德基金会下的独立研究机构，致力于让数据与 AI 服务于人与社会，开展关于生物识别与人脸识别的公众态度研究。

orgs.name: Adam Harvey
orgs.description: American artist-researcher of counter-surveillance whose CV Dazzle makeup defeats face detection, and whose Exposing.ai traced millions of photos scraped into face-recognition datasets.
orgs.description_zh: 美国反监控艺术家与研究者，CV Dazzle 妆容可骗过人脸检测，Exposing.ai 追踪了数以百万计被抓取进人脸识别数据集的照片。

orgs.name: Addie Wagenknecht
orgs.description: American artist whose Optimization of Parenthood uses a robot arm that rocks her baby's cradle when it cries, questioning what care becomes when it is automated.
orgs.description_zh: 美国艺术家，Optimization of Parenthood 中婴儿一哭，机械臂就会摇动摇篮，追问照护被自动化后会变成什么。

orgs.name: Adrian Mackenzie
orgs.description: Australian sociologist of technology whose Machine Learners reads machine-learning code and textbooks as a cultural practice, tracing how learning machines order the world.
orgs.description_zh: 澳大利亚技术社会学家，《机器学习者》把机器学习代码与教材当作文化实践来阅读，追踪学习机器如何整理世界。
known_for: Machine Learners: Archaeology of a Data Practice (2017)

orgs.name: Agnieszka Kurant
orgs.description: Polish artist of collective and non-human intelligence; A.A.I. consists of termite mounds built from coloured sand, 'artificial artificial intelligence' that echoes the crowdworkers behind AI.
orgs.description_zh: 波兰艺术家，关注集体智能与非人类智能；A.A.I. 由白蚁用彩色沙粒筑成的蚁丘构成，这种“人工的人工智能”呼应 AI 背后的众包工人。

orgs.name: Agnieszka Pilat
orgs.description: Polish-born painter who treats Boston Dynamics' Spot robots as studio companions and co-painters, staging machines as a new species learning to make marks.
orgs.description_zh: 波兰出生的画家，把波士顿动力的 Spot 机器狗当作画室伙伴与合作画家，把机器呈现为一个正在学习留下痕迹的新物种。

orgs.name: AI & Society (Springer)
orgs.description: Journal of knowledge, culture and communication on the societal implications of AI, including art, labour and ethics.
orgs.description_zh: 关于 AI 社会影响的知识、文化与传播期刊，涵盖艺术、劳动与伦理。

orgs.name: AI Art Gallery (aiartonline.com)
orgs.description: Online gallery of the NeurIPS Workshop on Machine Learning for Creativity and Design, curated by Luba Elliott, archiving the art selected by the ML community 2017–2021.
orgs.description_zh: 由 Luba Elliott 策划的 NeurIPS 机器学习与创意设计研讨会线上画廊，存档了 2017–2021 年机器学习社群选出的艺术作品。

orgs.name: AI Incident Database
orgs.description: Open archive of real-world harms and near-harms caused by AI systems, started at the Partnership on AI, which catalogues machine failures from misidentification to autonomous vehicle crashes.
orgs.description_zh: 记录 AI 系统在现实中造成或险些造成伤害的开放档案，起源于 Partnership on AI，收录从误识别到自动驾驶事故等各类机器失败。

orgs.name: AI Myths
orgs.description: Resource by Daniel Leufer debunking common misconceptions about AI, such as 'AI has agency' or 'AI can be objective', with references to research.
orgs.description_zh: 由 Daniel Leufer 创建的资源站，逐条拆解关于 AI 的常见误解（如“AI 具有能动性”“AI 可以客观”），并附研究文献。

orgs.name: AI Now Institute
orgs.description: Policy research institute co-founded by Kate Crawford and Meredith Whittaker on the social consequences of AI. Its reports on bias, labour and concentrated industry power shaped critical AI discourse.
orgs.description_zh: 由 Kate Crawford 与 Meredith Whittaker 共同创立的政策研究机构，研究 AI 的社会后果，其关于偏见、劳动与行业权力集中的报告塑造了批判性 AI 话语。

orgs.name: AI Weirdness
orgs.description: Janelle Shane's blog and newsletter on the strange ways AI fails, from neural-net paint colours to hallucinated giraffes: a long-running record of machine error as a window into machine 'minds'.
orgs.description_zh: Janelle Shane 的博客与通讯，记录 AI 各种奇特的失败，从神经网络命名的油漆颜色到凭空出现的长颈鹿，以机器错误为窗口观察机器“心智”。

orgs.name: AIAAIC Repository
orgs.description: Independent, public-interest repository of AI, algorithmic and automation incidents and controversies, classified by sector, technology and harm.
orgs.description_zh: 独立的公益性 AI、算法与自动化事件及争议资料库，按行业、技术与危害类型分类。

orgs.name: AIArtists.org
orgs.description: Directory of artists working with AI, organised by critical questions such as bias, dataset ethics and robotic production. It leans generative, so it is best used as a lead list.
orgs.description_zh: 与 AI 合作的艺术家名录，按偏见、数据集伦理、机器人创作等关键问题组织，偏重生成式作品，适合作为线索清单。

orgs.name: AIxDesign
orgs.description: Community and studio of designers, artists and researchers working critically with AI, running programmes, publications and a slow-AI research line.
orgs.description_zh: 由设计师、艺术家与研究者组成、以批判方式处理 AI 的社群与工作室，开展项目、出版物及“慢 AI”研究。
orgs.based_zh: 阿姆斯特丹，荷兰 / 全球

orgs.name: Akademie Schloss Solitude (Web Residencies)
orgs.description: Stuttgart residency academy whose online Web Residencies, published on Schlosspost, fund artists responding to curated calls, many on AI, bots and algorithmic culture.
orgs.description_zh: 斯图加特的驻留学院。其线上 Web Residencies 项目在 Schlosspost 发布，按策展主题资助艺术家，很多主题关于 AI、机器人程序与算法文化。

orgs.name: Aksioma – Institute for Contemporary Art
orgs.description: Ljubljana nonprofit that produces and publishes critical art on networks, algorithms and power, including the PostScriptUM publication series.
orgs.description_zh: 卢布尔雅那的非营利机构，制作并出版关于网络、算法与权力的批判性艺术，包括 PostScriptUM 出版系列。
orgs.based_zh: 卢布尔雅那，斯洛文尼亚

orgs.name: Alan Turing
orgs.description: British mathematician whose 1950 'imitation game' reframed the question 'can machines think?' as a performance judged by humans, the founding scene of AI.
orgs.description_zh: 英国数学家，1950 年提出“模仿游戏”，把“机器能思考吗”变成由人类评判的一场表演，这是人工智能的奠基场景。

orgs.name: Alexandra Daisy Ginsberg
orgs.description: British artist whose The Substitute brings back the last male northern white rhino as an AI-driven digital animal, asking why we prefer artificial life to the life we let die.
orgs.description_zh: 英国艺术家，The Substitute 以 AI 驱动的数字动物“复活”最后一头雄性北方白犀牛，追问为什么我们宁愿要人工生命，也任由真实的生命消亡。

orgs.name: Algorithmic Justice League
orgs.description: Organisation founded by Joy Buolamwini that combines art and research to expose bias in AI, starting from the 'coded gaze' of face recognition shown in Gender Shades.
orgs.description_zh: 由 Joy Buolamwini 创立的组织，结合艺术与研究揭示 AI 的偏见，起点是《Gender Shades》所揭示的人脸识别“编码凝视”。

orgs.name: AlgorithmWatch
orgs.description: Nonprofit research and advocacy organisation that investigates automated decision-making systems and their impact on society in Europe.
orgs.description_zh: 调查自动化决策系统及其对欧洲社会影响的非营利研究与倡导组织。

orgs.name: Amelie Klein
orgs.description: Curator at the Vitra Design Museum whose touring exhibition Hello, Robot. Design between Human and Machine surveyed robots from science fiction to smart homes.
orgs.description_zh: 维特拉设计博物馆策展人，其巡回展“你好，机器人：人与机器之间的设计”梳理了从科幻到智能家居的机器人。
known_for: Hello, Robot. Design between Human and Machine (Vitra Design Museum, 2017)

orgs.name: American Artist
orgs.description: American artist whose My Blue Window renders the city through a predictive-policing dashboard, confronting the racial logic of computational risk.
orgs.description_zh: 美国艺术家，My Blue Window 通过预测警务的仪表盘呈现城市，直面计算风险评估中的种族逻辑。

orgs.name: Anatomy of an AI System
orgs.description: Kate Crawford and Vladan Joler's map and essay of the human labour, data and planetary resources behind one Amazon Echo request; in the MoMA and V&A collections.
orgs.description_zh: Kate Crawford 与 Vladan Joler 绘制的地图与论文，揭示一次 Amazon Echo 请求背后的人类劳动、数据与地球资源，被 MoMA 与 V&A 收藏。

orgs.name: Andrew Norman Wilson
orgs.description: American artist who, while a contractor at Google, filmed the separately badged book-scanning workers, and then collected Google Books pages showing the scanners' fingers.
orgs.description_zh: 美国艺术家，在谷歌做合同工时拍摄了佩戴不同工牌的图书扫描工人，之后收集谷歌图书中留下扫描员手指的页面。

orgs.name: Andy Clark
orgs.description: British philosopher of the extended mind who argues that humans are 'natural-born cyborgs' whose thinking already runs through tools and machines.
orgs.description_zh: 英国哲学家，提出“延展心智”，主张人类是“天生的赛博格”，思维本就经由工具与机器运行。
known_for: The Extended Mind (1998, with David Chalmers)

orgs.name: Anicka Yi
orgs.description: Korean-American artist who 'biologises the machine': in In Love With the World, floating 'aerobes' drifted through Tate's Turbine Hall as a new machine species with their own sensing and behaviour.
orgs.description_zh: 韩裔美国艺术家，主张“让机器生物化”：在 In Love With the World 中，漂浮的“aerobes”作为有自身感知与行为的新机器物种在泰特涡轮大厅中游荡。
known_for: In Love With the World (Tate Turbine Hall, 2021)

orgs.name: Anna Munster
orgs.description: Australian theorist and artist who, with Adrian MacKenzie, developed 'platform seeing', a way to describe how machine vision operates at the scale of datasets and platforms.
orgs.description_zh: 澳大利亚理论家与艺术家，与 Adrian MacKenzie 提出“平台之看”，描述机器视觉如何在数据集与平台尺度上运作。

orgs.name: Anna Ridler
orgs.description: British artist who hand-builds her own datasets; Myriad (Tulips) displays 10,000 tulip photos she took and labelled, making visible the human labour and choices inside a training set.
orgs.description_zh: 英国艺术家，亲手构建自己的数据集；Myriad (Tulips) 展出她拍摄并逐一标注的一万张郁金香照片，让训练集中的人类劳动与选择变得可见。

orgs.name: Annie Dorsen
orgs.description: American theatre maker of 'algorithmic theatre'; in Hello Hi There two chatbots restage the Chomsky–Foucault debate on human nature, live and different each night.
orgs.description_zh: 美国剧场创作者，提出“算法剧场”；Hello Hi There 中两个聊天机器人每晚即兴重演乔姆斯基与福柯关于人性的辩论。

orgs.name: Antikythera
orgs.description: Think tank for the speculative philosophy of computation, directed by Benjamin Bratton and incubated at the Berggruen Institute. It studies planetary computation and synthetic intelligence through studios, publications and film.
orgs.description_zh: 由 Benjamin Bratton 主持、在博古睿研究院孵化的计算推测哲学智库，通过工作坊、出版与影片研究行星尺度计算与合成智能。

orgs.name: Antonio Somaini
orgs.description: Italian film and media theorist at Sorbonne Nouvelle who curated The World Through AI at the Jeu de Paume (2025), an exhibition on how AI sees, classifies and generates images.
orgs.description_zh: 新索邦大学意大利电影与媒介理论家，策划了网球场美术馆“AI 眼中的世界”（2025），探讨 AI 如何看、分类与生成图像。
known_for: The World Through AI (Le monde selon l'IA) (Jeu de Paume, 2025)
Algorithmic Images: Artificial Intelligence and Visual Culture (2023)

orgs.name: ANU School of Cybernetics
orgs.name_zh: 澳大利亚国立大学控制论学院
orgs.description: School founded by anthropologist Genevieve Bell, from the 3A Institute, to revive cybernetics as a way of building, steering and critiquing AI-enabled systems.
orgs.description_zh: 由人类学家 Genevieve Bell 基于 3A 研究所创办的学院，旨在复兴控制论，用于构建、驾驭与批判 AI 驱动的系统。

orgs.name: APRJA – A Peer-Reviewed Journal About
orgs.description: Open-access journal produced with transmediale and Aarhus University, each issue built from a research workshop on topics such as machine research and machine feeling.
orgs.description_zh: 与 transmediale 和奥胡斯大学合作的开放获取期刊，每期源自一场研究工作坊，主题如“机器研究”“机器感受”。

orgs.name: Archive of Digital Art (ADA)
orgs.description: Scholarly database of digital art founded by Oliver Grau, documenting hundreds of artists and thousands of works and texts, with strong coverage of robotic and A-life art.
orgs.description_zh: Oliver Grau 创立的数字艺术学术数据库，记录数百位艺术家及数千件作品与文献，对机器人与人工生命艺术覆盖尤深。

orgs.name: Ars Electronica Archive
orgs.description: Archive of Prix Ars Electronica entries since 1987, festival catalogues and documentation: the largest record of how media art engaged robots, A-life and AI.
orgs.description_zh: 收录 1987 年以来电子艺术大奖参赛作品、艺术节图录与文献的档案，是媒体艺术如何回应机器人、人工生命与 AI 的最大记录。

orgs.name: Ars Electronica Center
orgs.description: The 'museum of the future' of Ars Electronica. Its permanent exhibition Understanding AI (since 2019) shows how machines perceive and classify, with works such as Anatomy of an AI System and Gender Shades.
orgs.description_zh: 电子艺术节的“未来博物馆”。常设展《Understanding AI》（2019 年起）展示机器如何感知与分类，展出《Anatomy of an AI System》《Gender Shades》等作品。

orgs.name: Ars Electronica Festival
orgs.description: The world's longest-running festival for art, technology and society. Editions such as Artificial Intelligence – The Other I (2017), with its Artificial Intimacy section, set the agenda for machine art.
orgs.description_zh: 全球历史最悠久的艺术、技术与社会节。《Artificial Intelligence – The Other I》（2017，含“人工亲密”单元）等届次为机器艺术设定了议题。

orgs.name: Ars Electronica Futurelab
orgs.description: The R&D studio of Ars Electronica, working with industry and universities on drone swarms, robots and human-AI collaboration, and presenting the results as art.
orgs.description_zh: 电子艺术节的研发工作室，与企业和大学合作研究无人机群、机器人与人机协作，并以艺术形式呈现成果。

orgs.name: Art & Science International Exhibition and Symposium (Tsinghua)
orgs.name_zh: 艺术与科学国际作品展暨学术研讨会
orgs.description: Recurring exhibition and symposium initiated in 2001 at Tsinghua University by physicist T.D. Lee and painter Wu Guanzhong, now held at the Tsinghua University Art Museum. China's main art-and-science series.
orgs.description_zh: 2001 年由物理学家李政道与画家吴冠中在清华大学发起的系列展览与研讨会，现由清华大学艺术博物馆举办，是中国最主要的艺术与科学系列活动。

orgs.name: Art Center Nabi
orgs.description: Korea's first art centre dedicated to digital art, founded by SK Group. It has run robot art, AI and creative-technology programmes and hackathons for more than two decades.
orgs.description_zh: 韩国第一家数字艺术中心，由 SK 集团创办。二十多年来持续推出机器人艺术、AI 与创意技术项目以及黑客马拉松。

orgs.name: Arthur Ganson
orgs.description: American kinetic sculptor of gentle, philosophical machines; in Machine with Concrete a motor drives a chain of gears whose last one is set in concrete and would turn once in two trillion years.
orgs.description_zh: 美国动态雕塑家，作品温和而富哲思；Machine with Concrete 由电机带动一串齿轮，最后一个齿轮浇在混凝土里，需要两万亿年才会转一圈。

orgs.name: Artists + Machine Intelligence (Google AMI)
orgs.name_zh: 谷歌艺术家与机器智能计划
orgs.description: Google programme that pairs artists with machine intelligence researchers; it supported early DeepDream-era art and projects such as K Allado-McDowell's Pharmako-AI.
orgs.description_zh: 谷歌将艺术家与机器智能研究者配对的项目，支持了 DeepDream 时代的早期艺术以及 K Allado-McDowell 的《Pharmako-AI》等作品。

orgs.name: Atlas of Surveillance
orgs.description: EFF and University of Nevada, Reno database of surveillance technologies used by US police, from face recognition to drones and automated licence plate readers.
orgs.description_zh: 电子前哨基金会与内华达大学里诺分校合作的数据库，记录美国警方使用的监控技术，从人脸识别到无人机和自动车牌识别。

orgs.name: Auger & Loizeau (James Auger & Jimmy Loizeau)
orgs.description: British speculative designers whose Carnivorous Domestic Entertainment Robots feed on flies and mice to power themselves, re-imagining domestic robots as living things.
orgs.description_zh: 英国思辨设计师，Carnivorous Domestic Entertainment Robots 靠捕食苍蝇与老鼠供能，把家用机器人重新想象成有生命的东西。

orgs.name: Automato.farm
orgs.description: Design studio of Simone Rebaudengo, Matteo Loglio and Saurabh Datta; in Ethical Things a fan asks online crowdworkers to resolve its moral dilemmas.
orgs.description_zh: 由 Simone Rebaudengo、Matteo Loglio 和 Saurabh Datta 组成的设计工作室；Ethical Things 中的电风扇会请线上众包工人替它解决道德困境。
orgs.based_zh: 上海，中国 / 伦敦，英国

orgs.name: Ayoung Kim
orgs.description: South Korean artist whose Delivery Dancer's Sphere follows a female delivery rider in a Seoul run by an algorithmic platform that bends time and space.
orgs.description_zh: 韩国艺术家，《送货舞者之球》讲述一位女性外卖骑手在被算法平台支配、时空扭曲的首尔中穿行。

orgs.name: Barbican Centre
orgs.description: London arts centre whose exhibition AI: More than Human (2019) became a template for AI surveys, running from the dream of artificial beings through mind machines and data worlds.
orgs.description_zh: 伦敦的综合艺术中心。其展览《AI: More than Human》（2019）成为 AI 主题展的范本，从“人造生命之梦”一路讲到心智机器与数据世界。

orgs.name: Beijing Media Art Biennale
orgs.description: Biennale at the CAFA Art Museum, Central Academy of Fine Arts. Its first edition Ethics of Technology (2016) and Post-Life (2018) are key Chinese-language frames for art about machines.
orgs.description_zh: 由中央美术学院美术馆主办的双年展。首届《技术伦理》（2016）与第二届《后生命》（2018）是中文语境下机器艺术的重要框架。

orgs.name: Ben Grosser
orgs.description: American artist of software culture; Computers Watching Movies shows what a computer vision system 'looks at' in famous films, as sketched traces of machine attention.
orgs.description_zh: 美国软件文化艺术家；Computers Watching Movies 用草图般的轨迹呈现计算机视觉系统在经典电影中“看”的地方，描绘机器的注意力。

orgs.name: Benjamin Bratton
orgs.description: American theorist whose The Stack describes planetary computation as an accidental megastructure, and who argues AI should be understood as a new planetary intelligence.
orgs.description_zh: 美国理论家，《堆栈》把全球计算描述为意外形成的巨型结构，并主张把 AI 理解为一种新的行星尺度智能。

orgs.name: Bernard Stiegler
orgs.description: French philosopher who described technics as the 'exteriorised memory' that constitutes the human, and warned of an 'automatic society' of algorithmic governance.
orgs.description_zh: 法国哲学家，把技术描述为构成人类的“外在化记忆”，并警示算法治理下的“自动社会”。
known_for: Technics and Time, 1: The Fault of Epimetheus (1994)

orgs.name: Better Images of AI
orgs.description: Nonprofit collaboration offering a free library of images that represent AI more accurately than glowing brains and humanoid robots, commissioned from artists.
orgs.description_zh: 非营利合作项目，委托艺术家创作并免费提供比“发光大脑”和人形机器人更准确地表现 AI 的图像库。

orgs.name: Bill Vorn
orgs.description: Canadian robotic artist whose machines act out misery and hysteria: the octopus-like Hysterical Machines flail when visitors approach, provoking empathy for crude mechanisms.
orgs.description_zh: 加拿大机器人艺术家，他的机器上演痛苦与歇斯底里：章鱼状的 Hysterical Machines 在观众靠近时疯狂抽动，让人对粗糙的机构生出同情。
known_for: La Cour des Miracles (1997, with Louis-Philippe Demers)

orgs.name: Billy Klüver
orgs.description: Swedish Bell Labs engineer who built machines with Tinguely, Rauschenberg and Warhol and co-founded Experiments in Art and Technology, the model for artist–engineer collaboration.
orgs.description_zh: 瑞典裔贝尔实验室工程师，与 Tinguely、劳申伯格与沃霍尔合作制作机器，联合创立“艺术与技术实验”（E.A.T.），成为艺术家与工程师合作的典范。
known_for: Homage to New York (1960, with Jean Tinguely)
Experiments in Art and Technology (E.A.T., founded 1967)

orgs.name: Bjørn Karmann
orgs.description: Danish designer whose Project Alias is a fungus-like parasite that whispers noise into smart speakers until you wake it, and whose Paragraphica is a lensless camera that writes a photo from data.
orgs.description_zh: 丹麦设计师，Project Alias 像一只真菌寄生在智能音箱上，持续向它低语噪声直到你唤醒；Paragraphica 是一台没有镜头、用数据“写”出照片的相机。

orgs.name: Black in AI
orgs.description: Network co-founded by Timnit Gebru and Rediet Abebe to increase the presence and inclusion of Black people in AI.
orgs.description_zh: 由 Timnit Gebru 与 Rediet Abebe 共同发起的网络，旨在提升黑人在 AI 领域的参与和代表性。

orgs.name: Blake Lemoine
orgs.description: American engineer who was dismissed by Google in 2022 after publicly claiming that its LaMDA chatbot was sentient, a flashpoint for debates on machine interiority.
orgs.description_zh: 美国工程师，2022 年因公开声称谷歌聊天机器人 LaMDA 具有感知能力而被解雇，成为机器内在性争论的引爆点。

orgs.name: Blanca Li
orgs.description: Spanish choreographer whose Robot sets dancers alongside NAO humanoid robots and Maywa Denki's instruments, exploring how people and machines learn each other's movement.
orgs.description_zh: 西班牙编舞家，Robot 让舞者与 NAO 人形机器人及明和电机的乐器同台，探索人与机器如何学习彼此的动作。

orgs.name: Blast Theory
orgs.description: British artist group of interactive performance; Cat Royale (2023) watched a robot arm try to entertain three cats for twelve days, asking whether machines can care for other species.
orgs.description_zh: 英国互动表演团体；Cat Royale（2023）记录一只机械臂连续十二天试图取悦三只猫，追问机器能否照顾其他物种。

orgs.name: Blood in the Machine
orgs.description: Brian Merchant's newsletter and book on the Luddites and today's fight against automation, reporting how AI reshapes work.
orgs.description_zh: Brian Merchant 的通讯与同名著作，讲述卢德派与当下反自动化的抗争，报道 AI 如何重塑工作。

orgs.name: Bruce Lacey
orgs.description: British artist of anarchic, junk-built robots and performing automata, several shown at Cybernetic Serendipity (1968); his humanoid machines were deliberately comic, clumsy and vulnerable.
orgs.description_zh: 英国艺术家，用废品拼装出无政府气质的机器人与表演自动机，多件曾在“控制论的意外发现”（1968）展出；他的类人机器刻意滑稽、笨拙而脆弱。

orgs.name: Calculating Empires
orgs.description: Large-scale research visualisation by Crawford and Joler, A Genealogy of Technology and Power 1500–2025, tracing how communication and computation systems grew with control; S+T+ARTS Grand Prize 2024.
orgs.description_zh: Crawford 与 Joler 的大型研究可视化《技术与权力的谱系 1500–2025》，追溯通信与计算系统如何与控制一同扩张，获 2024 年 S+T+ARTS 大奖。

orgs.name: Cao Fei
orgs.description: Chinese artist of labour, virtual worlds and automation; Asia One follows the only two workers in a fully automated logistics warehouse, falling in love among sorting robots.
orgs.description_zh: 中国艺术家，关注劳动、虚拟世界与自动化；《亚洲一号》讲述全自动物流仓库中仅有的两名工人在分拣机器人之间相恋。

orgs.name: Carnegie Museum of Art (Hillman Photography Initiative)
orgs.description: Pittsburgh museum whose Hillman Photography Initiative ran Mirror with a Memory (2020–21), a programme on AI, photography, surveillance and bias, including Trevor Paglen's Opposing Geometries.
orgs.description_zh: 匹兹堡的艺术博物馆。其 Hillman 摄影计划推出《Mirror with a Memory》（2020–21），探讨 AI、摄影、监控与偏见，包括 Trevor Paglen 的《Opposing Geometries》。

orgs.name: Caroline Sinders
